result:
The proposed answer of 0 is wrong. The correct limit is $e^{-\lambda}$.

The error is in counting codewords rather than projective codewords. Each bad line through the origin contributes $q-1$ nonzero codewords, so the expected number of weight-$(n-k)$ codewords overcounts by a factor of about $q$. The number of projective weight-$(n-k)$ codewords has expectation

$$\frac{\mathbb{E}[N_{n-k}]}{q-1} \approx \frac{\binom{n}{k}\,(q-1)^{n-k}q^{k-n}}{q-1} \approx \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{q} \to \lambda,$$

which is finite, not $q\lambda \to \infty$. Lower weights $w < n-k$ have expectations $\approx \binom{n}{w}q^{w-1+k-n}$, which tend to 0 because $n \ll q$ in this regime.

A direct check agrees. The code is MDS iff every $k$ columns of the generator matrix are linearly independent, i.e. all $\binom{n}{k}$ maximal minors are nonzero. Each minor vanishes with probability about $1/q$, so the expected number of vanishing minors is about $\binom{n}{k}/q \to \lambda$. The bad events are approximately independent and rare, so the count is approximately Poisson($\lambda$), giving $\Pr[\text{MDS}] \to e^{-\lambda}$.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
